BOOKING DOC REVIEW (S235 Gate 0.5, read-only). Sources read: ERD v2 README + booking.dbml, inquiry.submitted.v1.json, ADR 0001/0002/0003, schema-ownership.md, tripplanner-to-aaa-handoff.md, ecosystem-architecture.md, ecosystem-review-2026-09.md, the PRD PDF (15 pages, text-extracted with pypdf into the scratchpad because poppler is missing), AAA_Quanskill_Handover_Review.docx, the figma_AAA listing (120 PNGs, 2 opened), AA-CIS-Infra (CONTEXT, cicd.tf, tripplanner.tf, modules/ecs|alb|api_gateway, db-migrate.yml, db/run_migration.py), AA-CIS-App CONTEXT + ci.yml/deploy-dev.yml, db-schema-reference.md, Linear AA-677/678/679/680/683/751 (plus the AA-678 comment).

WHAT IS DECIDED (good enough to build on)
1. Placement: acc2, same RDS, schema `booking`, no new account or region (ADR 0001 decisions 6-7, docs/adr/0001-ecosystem-target-architecture.md:56-57,67-68; review §10 docs/architecture/ecosystem-review-2026-09.md:501; AA-678 "Decisions").
2. Ownership and migrations: AA-Booking owns `booking.*`, key `bk-NNN` (docs/database/schema-ownership.md:31,47). Migrations are applied by AA-CIS-Infra DB Migrate from a byte-identical copy. The workflow ALREADY accepts `booking/NNN_name.sql` and maps it to `bk-NNN` (infra/AA-CIS-Infra/.github/workflows/db-migrate.yml:52-61; db/README.md:9-13). Self-registration goes into `shared.schema_versions(version, description, applied_at)` (db-schema-reference.md:1079-1084; run_migration.py:35-47).
3. Content boundary: only CIS writes content. Booking reads views and writes only its own schema, enforced by its own DB role (docs/adr/0002-only-cis-writes-content.md:34,39,42,55).
4. Transport: an in-DB transactional outbox. The TripPlanner side exists: `tripplanner.outbox` + `v_inquiry_outbox` (apps/AA-TripPlanner-Web/migrations/008_inquiry_outbox.sql:20-39). Its header says the grant to Booking's role is added "when that role exists (AA-678)" (008:10-11). The consumer side is `booking.inbox_events` (booking.dbml:596-606).
5. Contract inquiry.submitted v1 is published (docs/contracts/inquiry.submitted.v1.json) with idempotency_key `<trip_id>:<handoff_id>` (line 12) and the leg chain (lines 41-56).
6. ERD v2 closes the handover P0/P1 gaps: media_files, supplier_bookings/bills, payment_schedule, audit_logs, a 13-value status enum, audit and soft-delete columns. It answers the 6 business questions (docs/AAA/erd-v2/README.md:35-43,89-102).
7. Customer identity: Booking owns OTP (ADR 0001:65). OTP is done once per device, then a 30-day refresh-token session (README.md:97).
8. Stack, as a proposal only: FastAPI + asyncpg backend, Next.js frontend, ECS service `aa-booking-dev-api` on `aa-cis-dev-cluster`, OIDC sub `repo:AdventureAsia365-Ecosys*/AA-Booking*:*`, Terraform in `accounts/aa365` (Linear AA-678 description). Review §7 recommends the same (ecosystem-review-2026-09.md:449-451), but its open question 5 is still listed (line 551). No ADR records it yet, so ADR 0004 below closes it.
9. Harness baseline asked by Nghiệp on AA-678 (comment 06/10): deploy guard + post-deploy smoke + api/worker same SHA; trip-case state machine enforced in the DB; idempotency keys on every side-effecting endpoint; least-privilege DB role.

WHAT IS MISSING / UNDECIDED
A. Staff identity. Four sources disagree (see contradictions): ERD v2 table `booking.staff_users`, AA-680 "no separate staff user store", CIS `shared.admin_users` (username + password_hash, db-schema-reference.md:675-684), and Figma password reset (figma_AAA/RESET PASSWORD.png). This must be decided before any staff-facing table.
B. How the DB role is created. No repo contains `CREATE ROLE tripplanner`. The only CREATE ROLE in any repo is CIS 007b `aa_app_user` (apps/AA-CIS-App/api/migrations/007b_create_app_user.sql:25). Infra "owns DB roles" (schema-ownership.md:20-23) but has no SQL owner key in DB Migrate (only cis|tripplanner|booking, db-migrate.yml:52). The password and secret flow for a new login role is not written down anywhere.
C. API exposure. There is no Booking listener rule, target group or API route. The VPC-link NLB forwards to the ALB on port 80 (modules/alb/vpc_link.tf:78-86). The ALB HTTP listener default-forwards to the CIS target group (modules/alb/main.tf:74-84), and the alb module exports only `https_listener_arn` (modules/alb/outputs.tf). The API GW custom domain is a single `aa_cis` domain from tfvars `api-cis-aa365.lumiguides.it.com` (accounts/aa365/terraform.tfvars:25-26; modules/api_gateway/main.tf:512-525), while the live endpoint in CLAUDE.md is `api-cis.lumiguides.it.com`, so domain/cert coverage for a Booking hostname is unknown.
D. No `catalog.tour.v1` contract and no CIS catalog views exist (AA-679 names `docs/contracts/catalog.tour.v1.json`, which is not in docs/contracts/). There is no country ISO mapping: `shared.destinations.country` is free text (db-schema-reference.md:752-760) and README.md:109-111 leaves it open. This blocks trip_plans, activities, hotels and destination_profiles.
E. Guest hand-off. The contract allows `customer: null` (inquiry.submitted.v1.json:17-18), but `booking.trip_cases.customer_id` is NOT NULL (booking.dbml:337).
F. Job runner for the inbox consumer. ADR 0001 says "consumed by the receiving app's job runner" (0001:57). ADR 0003 rule 4 defers a second enqueuing repo (0003:55-58), and AA-751 is Backlog with kind prefix `aab_*`. Also, the CIS Deploy Dev guard counts every queued/running `shared.job` row (deploy-dev.yml:29-60), so Booking kinds would block CIS deploys unless the guard filters by kind.
G. OTP delivery. No SES/SMS exists. The TripPlanner advisor notify is still a logging stub (tripplanner-to-aaa-handoff.md:33-34). This blocks AA-680, not the bootstrap.
H. Customer app scope. PRD §7 has a customer app with map Discovery, Inquiry, My Trips and My Payments (PRD p.14). AA-678 plans "two surfaces: staff admin and customer app". TripPlanner is already the B2C map discovery + inquiry front. Nobody has decided whether Booking builds discovery or only My Trips / My Payments.
I. The PRD has no API spec, no NFRs, no payment provider (payments are marked manually, PRD p.6 "Admin marks payments as received"), no currency or i18n rule, and no notification channels. Its sections jump from 2 to 4 and from 5 to 7 (PRD p.7-8, p.13-14), so sections 3 and 6 are missing.
J. Trip case code format is not specified. Figma shows `#TC-2024-089` and templates `#TP-2024-089` (figma_AAA/TRIP CASES MANAGEMENT.png).
K. The design-system package (ADR 0001 decision 7, "one token source") does not exist yet. The CIS kit lives inside the CIS app at frontend/app/_kit (apps/AA-CIS-App/CONTEXT.md:62-73). A Booking frontend would have to copy it for now.
L. ADR 0001 is still "Status: Proposed" (0001:3), yet every later doc treats it as locked (skill/ai-nghiep/references/adr.md "Đã khoá" table).

ARCHITECT VERDICT: the docs are sufficient to bootstrap the repo, CI, Infra, DB role, `bk-001` (foundation + identity + intake core) and the health endpoint now. They are NOT sufficient for catalog sync (D), staff-facing screens (A) or guest intake (E). Those stay out of bk-001.
contradictions: Region/accounts: ecosystem-review-2026-09.md:208 (diagram 'AA-Booking · AAA accounts ap-southeast-1') and :446 ('Terraform ... new roots accounts/aaa-{dev,stg,prod}') contradict ADR 0001:67-68 + review §10 :501 (same acc2, no new accounts). The body of the review was never updated after the 28/09 decision; global CLAUDE.md still lists AAA DEV/STG/PROD accounts 710590321660/593110023608/007050358335 in ap-southeast-1, which review :166 says are closed.

Transport: ecosystem-review-2026-09.md:214 and §6.2 :416-419 (signed HMAC webhook, Idempotency-Key = draft_id + revision) contradict ADR 0001:56-57 and handoff :43-58 (in-DB transactional outbox; webhook superseded). The idempotency key also differs: review 'draft_id + revision' vs contract '<trip_id>:<handoff_id>' (inquiry.submitted.v1.json:12).

Golden records: ecosystem-review-2026-09.md:442-443 and Linear AA-677 item 2 ('countries/areas/destinations reference shared.destinations / a new shared.countries owned by CIS'; external_ref on destinations and countries) vs ERD v2 README.md:21-25 (country_profiles keyed by ISO code stored in booking, destination_profiles keyed by CIS id, no shared.countries). The ISO mapping question is left open at README.md:109-111.

Staff identity (4-way): ERD v2 booking.dbml:163-173 creates booking.staff_users (email, role, no password); README.md:50-52 says staff 'use the ecosystem staff model from AA-656'; Linear AA-680 says 'No separate staff user store per app'; CIS's actual staff model is shared.admin_users with username + password_hash (db-schema-reference.md:675-684; apps/AA-CIS-App/CONTEXT.md:286-290) and roles admin/reviewer/content, not admin/sales/content_creator (CONTEXT.md:304-307). Figma 'RESET PASSWORD.png' shows email reset links / temporary passwords and a 'Super Admin' role, which the handover rule 'OTP-only auth — no password field' (Handover Review §2.3) and the staff_role enum (booking.dbml:18-22) do not cover.
OTP session: booking.dbml:160 still says 'proposed, TO CONFIRM' on customer_sessions while README.md:91-97 says the 6 questions are decided (S226).

Contracts folder: README.md:107-108 ('docs/contracts/ (not created yet)') and ecosystem-architecture.md:156 ('folder not created yet') are stale; docs/contracts/inquiry.submitted.v1.json exists and handoff :136-138 marks it done.
AAA source path: tripplanner-to-aaa-handoff.md:7-9 and :158 point to apps/AA-TripPlanner-Web/docs/AAA/, which no longer exists; the files are in docs/AAA/.

Guest hand-off: inquiry.submitted.v1.json:17-18 allows customer = null ('guest hand-off'), but booking.dbml:337 makes trip_cases.customer_id NOT NULL and PRD p.2 says an inquiry always creates a customer account.

Tour id type: published_tours.tour_id is uuid (db-schema-reference.md:582-585) and booking.dbml:367 types trip_case_legs.source_tour_id as uuid, but the contract types source_tour_id as an unconstrained string (inquiry.submitted.v1.json:50,74) and TripPlanner stores it as TEXT (apps/AA-TripPlanner-Web/migrations/001_tripplanner_schema.sql:23). The consumer must validate and cast.

Trip-case statuses: PRD p.4 says 'no need for V1 Sent / V2 Sent ... Better status: Building → Confirmed', while PRD p.8 lists 'V1,V2,V3 (building, sent)'; ERD v2 encodes both building and proposal_sent (booking.dbml:29-43); Figma TRIP CASES MANAGEMENT.png uses a different 6-value vocabulary (Draft / In Progress / Sent / Approved / Completed / Cancelled).

Content authoring: PRD p.7-8 gives Content Creator 'Create/Edit/Delete/Draft activity', and PRD p.15 + Figma (ADD COUNTRY, ADD DESTINATION, DELETE DESTINATION screens) let AAA staff manage countries and destinations. ADR 0002:34-41 says content is written only by CIS, and ADR 0002:55 says AA-Booking reads views only. ERD v2 keeps manual activities (source_system 'manual', is_draft, booking.dbml:242-260) and country FAQ / festivals / weather text (booking.dbml:185-199) without a ruling on whether that is 'content' or 'commercial data'.

View-only reads: ADR 0002:34 says other apps read content 'through published views, never the tables', but ERD v2 FKs point at the table shared.destinations (booking.dbml:202,230,248) and TripPlanner reads that table directly via grant (CIS 201). No shared.v_destinations view exists.

Orders: ADR 0002:39-41 says AA-Booking writes 'cases, orders and payments' and PRD p.5-6 names a 'Confirmed Trip Order' / 'Order / Trip → final record', but ERD v2 has no order table (the approved trip_case_version is the order, README.md:76).

Migration practice: apps/AA-CIS-App/CONTEXT.md:256-259 says migrations are applied 'by hand through ECS exec', while schema-ownership.md:20-23, Infra CONTEXT.md:148-152 and db/README.md say they go only through the DB Migrate workflow (S225). The CIS CONTEXT line is stale and would mislead a Booking implementer copying CIS.
Catalog lineage naming: apps/AA-CIS-App/CONTEXT.md:276 and Linear AA-679 say 'idempotent by external_ref', while ERD v2 uses the column pair (source_system, source_id) (booking.dbml:249-259,275-286).

Customer identity owner: ADR 0001:65 and AA-680 make Booking the customer identity owner with TripPlanner's registration.py as a client, but the contract carries tripplanner.customers.id as customer_id (inquiry.submitted.v1.json:26), so two customer stores keep existing and are matched only by phone/email (booking.dbml:139).
Job kind prefix: Linear AA-751 namespaces Booking job kinds as `aab_*`, while the schema key convention is `bk-`. Pick one before the first kind.

ADR status: docs/adr/0001-ecosystem-target-architecture.md:3 is still 'Proposed (28/09/2026) ... Accepted once Nghiệp signs off', yet skill/ai-nghiep/references/adr.md lists root 0001 under 'Đã khoá' (locked) and every Booking doc cites it as decided.
stack_proposal:
STACK PROPOSAL (consistent with ADR 0001/0002/0003 and CIS conventions). Full text is in the ADR draft. Summary:

1. Language/framework: copy CIS where it is proven.
   - Backend: Python 3.12 + FastAPI + Pydantic v2 + asyncpg with plain SQL repositories, no ORM in the request path (CIS: Dockerfile FROM python:3.12-slim; requirements fastapi>=0.110.1, asyncpg==0.29.0, pydantic>=2.8.0).
   - Frontend: Next.js 16 / React 19 / TypeScript + @tanstack/react-query + @tanstack/react-table, the same as CIS frontend/package.json. It starts as a copy of CIS app/_kit + _brand/tokens until the shared design-system package (AA-655) exists. It deploys to Vercel.
   - Rejected: Laravel/PHP. The handover's 'Spatie' tables imply Quanskill's stack was Laravel, but no code was delivered and the team has no PHP CI/deploy path. Rejected: Lambda like TripPlanner, because OTP sessions, the inbox consumer and staff CRUD fit a long-running service and the ECS + DB Migrate path already exists.

2. Repo `AdventureAsia365-Ecosys/AA-Booking`:
   - backend/: package `app` with main.py, routers/health.py, db.py (asyncpg pool from DATABASE_URL), settings.py, tests/unit, tests/integration, plus pyproject.toml, requirements.txt and Dockerfile.
   - migrations/NNN_*.sql: owner key bk-NNN, same placement as TripPlanner's top-level migrations/.
   - frontend/: Next.js staff admin first. The customer surface waits for the scope decision.
   - docs/: adr/0001-implements-root-0004.md, erd/ (ERD v2 moved from root docs/AAA/erd-v2 per README.md:3-4), ui-spec.md (AA-683).
   - Root files: CONTEXT.md, README.md, .claude/CLAUDE.md, all in English from day one (AA-678).

3. CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) has 5 required checks, named like CIS so branch protection mirrors it:
   - Lint: ruff, failing.
   - Security Audit: pip-audit, failing on findings, unlike CIS `|| true`.
   - Unit Tests: pytest. Includes a migration guard test: every migrations/*.sql has BEGIN/COMMIT, inserts its own 'bk-NNN' into shared.schema_versions with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, and creates or alters nothing outside schema `booking`.
   - Integration Tests: postgres:15 service. Creates a stub `shared` schema (schema_versions + destinations + v_tour_photos), applies migrations/*.sql in order, then hits /booking/health/ready.
   - Docker Build Check: plus Trivy report-only and an SBOM, as in CIS.
   - Non-required: Frontend Build (`next build` + eslint). Later: UI smoke on Vercel preview (AA-732 pattern).
   - Also a Migration Copy Check: optional and non-required, compares sha256 with AA-CIS-Infra/db/migrations/booking/ via the GitHub API.

4. Deploy path (`deploy-dev.yml`, on push to main + workflow_dispatch):
   - OIDC with a dedicated least-privilege role `aa-booking-dev-app-deploy`, NOT aa-cis-dev-role.
   - Build and push to ECR `aa-booking-dev-api` with an immutable git-sha tag.
   - Register a task definition from the current one (only the image swapped), update service `aa-booking-dev-api`, wait services-stable, verify the running taskDef image SHA.
   - Smoke: curl /booking/health (200, {status, service, git_sha}) and /booking/health/ready (200, {db:'ok', schema_version:'bk-001'}).
   - The job guard is not needed until Booking has jobs, and then it must filter on its own kinds.
   - The frontend deploys via Vercel Git integration.

5. Runtime (Terraform in AA-CIS-Infra `accounts/aa365/booking.tf`, the tripplanner.tf pattern; CIS resources stay untouched):
   - Fargate service `aa-booking-dev-api` on the existing `aa-cis-dev-cluster`: 0.25 vCPU / 0.5 GB, FARGATE_SPOT weighted, circuit breaker + rollback, ignore_changes on task_definition/desired_count, enable_execute_command.
   - Own exec role and task role (no Bedrock, no CIS secrets), log group `/ecs/aa-booking-dev`, secret `booking/dev/database-url`.
   - ALB target group :8000 with health check /booking/health.
   - `aws_lb_listener_rule` path `/booking/*` on the ALB HTTP listener. This needs a new alb module output `http_listener_arn`, because the NLB→ALB hop is on port 80.
   - A separate REST API `aa-booking-dev` reusing the existing VPC link, proxying `/booking/{proxy+}` to `http://<nlb>/booking/{proxy}`.
   - A custom domain `api-booking.lumiguides.it.com` only if the ACM cert covers it; otherwise the execute-api URL for Dev.
   - No worker service until the first job kind (AA-751).

6. Database:
   - Login role `booking`: USAGE+CREATE on schema `booking` and all rights on its objects. No rights on other schemas until owners grant them: CIS migration 223 (shared.destinations, shared.v_tour_photos, shared.v_destination_photos, later catalog views) and TripPlanner tp-009 (tripplanner.v_inquiry_outbox).
   - No shared.job and no shared.llm_call_log grants until needed.
   - bk-001 creates the schema, the guarded NOLOGIN role, grants, default privileges, enums and the first-slice tables.
   - The file is byte-copied to AA-CIS-Infra/db/migrations/booking/001_<name>.sql and applied by DB Migrate (check → apply). Repeat for each bk-NNN.

7. ADR placement: root `AA-Ecosys/docs/adr/0004-aa-booking-stack-and-bootstrap.md`. Reversing it touches AA-Booking, AA-CIS-Infra and the CIS/TP grant migrations. AA-Booking's own docs/adr/0001 cites it.
adr_draft_markdown:
# ADR 0004 — AA-Booking: stack, repo layout, runtime and bootstrap on acc2

- **Status:** Proposed (14/10/2026, S235 Gate 0.5 — architect draft). Accepted once Nghiệp signs off decisions 1–9 and the open decisions in the last section.
- **Scope:** AA-Ecosys (new repo AA-Booking, AA-CIS-Infra, AA-CIS-App and AA-TripPlanner-Web for the read grants).
- **Implements:** ADR 0001 decisions 5–7 (placement, contracts, one IaC repo), ADR 0002 (only CIS writes content), ADR 0003 (one durable job model). Closes ecosystem review §11 open question 5 ("Does AAA follow the CIS stack?").
- **Related:** AA-677 (ERD v2, done), AA-678 (bootstrap), AA-679 (catalog sync), AA-680 (identity), AA-681 (trip case), AA-682 (operations), AA-683 (UI spec), AA-751 (second repo on `shared.job`).

## Context

AA-Booking (AAA) is built in-house from scratch (Nghiệp, 28/09 and S226). The inputs are the Quanskill PRD (09/06/2026), the v1 ERD, the handover review (10/06/2026), about 110 Figma screens and ERD v2 (`docs/AAA/erd-v2/`). No vendor code was delivered. ADR 0001 fixes where Booking runs: acc2, the shared RDS, schema `booking`, provisioned by AA-CIS-Infra, with no new accounts. It does not fix how Booking is built.

What already exists:
- **DB Migrate** accepts `booking/NNN_*.sql` and registers `bk-NNN` (`AA-CIS-Infra/.github/workflows/db-migrate.yml`).
- TripPlanner writes `inquiry.submitted` v1 into `tripplanner.outbox` and exposes `tripplanner.v_inquiry_outbox` (tp-008).
- CIS runs FastAPI + asyncpg on ECS behind API Gateway (REST) → VPC link → NLB → ALB, deploys through GitHub OIDC, and enforces "done" as merge + CI + rollout COMPLETED + live verify.

What it costs to differ from CIS: a second CI, deploy, auth and testing toolchain for a solo-run program.

## Decisions

1. **Stack = the CIS stack.**
   - Backend: Python 3.12, FastAPI, Pydantic v2, asyncpg with plain SQL repositories (no ORM in request paths).
   - Frontend: Next.js 16 / React 19 / TypeScript with `@tanstack/react-query` and `@tanstack/react-table`.
   - Database: PostgreSQL 15 on the shared RDS.
   - The frontend copies the CIS UI kit (`app/_kit`) and brand tokens until the shared design-system package (ADR 0001 decision 7, AA-655) is published, then switches to it.

2. **Repo `AdventureAsia365-Ecosys/AA-Booking`, layout:**
   ```
   backend/        FastAPI app (app/main.py, app/routers/, app/db.py, app/settings.py), tests/unit, tests/integration, Dockerfile
   migrations/     NNN_<name>.sql — owner key bk-NNN
   frontend/       Next.js — staff admin first; customer surface after the scope decision (open decision 4)
   docs/adr/       repo ADRs; 0001 cites this ADR
   docs/erd/       ERD v2 (moved from AA-Ecosys/docs/AAA/erd-v2)
   CONTEXT.md, README.md, .claude/CLAUDE.md   (English)
   ```
   - Trunk-based (ADR-2026-023): feature branch → PR → required CI → human merge to `main`.
   - Commits follow the program format (`feat|fix|chore|refactor|docs: …` + `Refs AA-xxx`).

3. **CI: five required checks**, mirroring CIS names so branch protection reads the same:
   - **Lint** (ruff).
   - **Security Audit** (pip-audit, failing, unlike CIS's report-only).
   - **Unit Tests**, including a migration guard: each `migrations/*.sql` is wrapped in `BEGIN; … COMMIT;`, registers its own `bk-NNN` with `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`, and creates or alters nothing outside schema `booking`.
   - **Integration Tests**: Postgres 15 service with a stub `shared` schema; apply all migrations in order, then call `/booking/health/ready`.
   - **Docker Build Check**, with a Trivy report and an SBOM.
   - Non-required: **Frontend Build** (`next build` + eslint). Later: UI smoke on Vercel preview (AA-732 pattern).

4. **Deploy path.**
   - `deploy-dev.yml` on push to `main`.
   - GitHub OIDC → role `aa-booking-dev-app-deploy`. This role is new and least-privilege: ECR push to `aa-booking-dev-api` only, `ecs:RegisterTaskDefinition`/`DescribeTaskDefinition`, `UpdateService`/`DescribeServices` on Booking services only, and `iam:PassRole` on the two Booking roles only. AA-Booking never receives the broad `aa-cis-dev-role` ARN.
   - Image tag = git SHA (immutable).
   - Register a new task definition from the current one (only the image swapped), update the service, wait `services-stable`, and verify that the running image SHA equals the commit.
   - Smoke: `GET /booking/health` → 200 `{status, service, git_sha}` and `GET /booking/health/ready` → 200 `{db:"ok", schema_version:"bk-001"}`.
   - Once Booking owns job kinds, add a pre-deploy guard on its own kinds (AA-725 pattern).
   - Frontend: Vercel Git integration.
   - "Done" follows `aa-ship`: merge + CI + rollout COMPLETED + live verify.

5. **Runtime, provisioned by AA-CIS-Infra** in a self-contained `accounts/aa365/booking.tf` (the `tripplanner.tf` pattern; no existing CIS resource modified except one new alb module output):
   - ECR `aa-booking-dev-api` (scan on push, keep last 10).
   - Log group `/ecs/aa-booking-dev`.
   - Own execution role (GetSecretValue on `booking/dev/*` only) and own task role. No Bedrock and no CIS secrets; add only when a feature needs them.
   - Secret `booking/dev/database-url`: a placeholder in Terraform with `ignore_changes`; the value is set out-of-band.
   - ECS service `aa-booking-dev-api` on the existing `aa-cis-dev-cluster`:
     - 0.25 vCPU / 0.5 GB, FARGATE base 1 + FARGATE_SPOT;
     - circuit breaker with rollback;
     - `ignore_changes = [task_definition, desired_count]`;
     - `enable_execute_command`;
     - existing private subnets and app security group.
   - Routing:
     - ALB target group (port 8000, health check `/booking/health`);
     - listener rule `path-pattern /booking/*` on the ALB **HTTP** listener (the NLB → ALB hop is port 80), which needs a new `http_listener_arn` output in `modules/alb`;
     - a separate REST API `aa-booking-dev` reusing the existing VPC link: `ANY /booking/{proxy+}` → `http://<nlb>/booking/{proxy}`;
     - custom domain `api-booking.lumiguides.it.com` if the ACM certificate covers it; otherwise the execute-api URL for Dev until a certificate is issued.
   - A worker service is added only with the first job kind (decision 8).
   - Rough cost: one 0.25 vCPU / 0.5 GB Fargate task, mostly on Spot, is a few USD per month. No new ALB, NLB or NAT.
   - IAM bootstrap order: first add a `BookingRoleTagging` statement (`iam:TagRole`/`UntagRole` on `role/aa-booking-dev-*`) to `aa-cis-dev-role` and apply it. Only then apply `booking.tf` (same propagation trap as `TripPlannerRoleTagging`).

6. **Database role and grants (ADR 0002 decision 4 in the database).**
   - Login role `booking`: rights only on schema `booking`.
   - Reads outside its schema are granted only by the owner, in the owner's migration, guarded `IF EXISTS (role booking)`:
     - CIS migration (next number, e.g. 223): `USAGE` on `shared` + `SELECT` on `shared.v_tour_photos`, `shared.v_destination_photos` and `shared.destinations` (a view `shared.v_destinations` is preferred if CIS adds one), plus the catalog views when AA-679 defines them;
     - TripPlanner `tp-009`: `USAGE` on `tripplanner` + `SELECT` on `tripplanner.v_inquiry_outbox`.
   - Booking gets no `shared.job` grant before AA-751 and no `shared.llm_call_log` grant before it calls an LLM.
   - Role creation: `bk-001` creates `booking` **NOLOGIN** if it is missing, so the file is self-contained and idempotent. A one-off approved step then sets `LOGIN PASSWORD` from the value stored in `booking/dev/database-url`. No password is ever in Git.

7. **Migrations.**
   - Authored in `AA-Booking/migrations/NNN_*.sql`, key `bk-NNN`.
   - A byte-identical copy goes in `AA-CIS-Infra/db/migrations/booking/NNN_*.sql`.
   - Applied to Dev by **DB Migrate** (`check` → `apply`) from `main` of AA-CIS-Infra, before any app code that needs it merges.
   - `docs/architecture/db-schema-reference.md` is regenerated after each structural migration.
   - `bk-001` is a **first slice**, not the whole ERD v2:
     - schema, role, grants, default privileges;
     - enums `record_status`, `staff_role` (if open decision 1 keeps a Booking staff table), `trip_case_status`, `source_system`;
     - identity: `customers`, `customer_otps`, `customer_sessions`, and `staff_users` subject to open decision 1;
     - geography: `areas`, `country_profiles`, `media_files`;
     - intake core: `trip_cases` (without `trip_plan_id`), `trip_case_countries`, `trip_case_legs`, `trip_case_status_history`, a `trip_case_status_transitions` table + trigger that rejects illegal status jumps (AA-678 harness comment);
     - cross-cutting: `inbox_events` (unique on `(source, contract, idempotency_key)`), `audit_logs`.

     Catalog and inventory tables (`suppliers`, `hotels`, `activities`, `trip_plans*`, `destination_profiles`, `entity_media`) follow in `bk-002`, after the `catalog.tour.v1` contract and the country ISO decision. Versions, operations and money tables (`trip_case_versions*`, `trip_case_checks`, `staff_assignments`, `supplier_*`, `invoices`, `invoice_items`, `payment_schedule`, `payments`, `notifications`) follow in `bk-003` with AA-681/682. Reason: PostgreSQL enum values cannot be removed or renamed cheaply, and several FKs depend on undecided contracts.

8. **Deferred work uses the one job model (ADR 0003).**
   - `inbox_events` is the durable record of what was consumed.
   - Processing (inquiry intake, later catalog sync and notifications) runs as `shared.job` kinds in the Booking namespace once AA-751 grants Booking `INSERT`/`SELECT` on its own kinds. They run on a Booking-owned worker service (same image, `python -m worker`) that claims only Booking kinds.
   - The CIS Deploy Dev guard must then filter on CIS kinds, so Booking work does not block CIS deploys, and the reverse.
   - No in-process `asyncio.create_task` in request paths.

9. **Health and readiness are separate.**
   - `/booking/health` = process liveness, with no DB call. The ALB health check uses it, so a DB outage or a missing grant cannot trip the ECS circuit breaker into a rollback loop.
   - `/booking/health/ready` = DB connectivity + `bk-001` present in `shared.schema_versions`. Smoke tests and alarms use it.

## Open decisions (must be answered at Gate 1)

1. **Staff identity.**
   - (a) One store: Booking staff log in through the CIS staff login (`shared.admin_users`, AA-656). `booking.staff_users` becomes a thin profile keyed by `admin_users.id` (Booking role `admin|sales|content_creator`, no password).
   - (b) Booking keeps its own `staff_users` with its own auth.
   - Recommended: (a). It matches AA-680 "no separate staff user store". It needs a CIS migration adding email and the Booking roles, or a role-mapping table, and a token-verification contract.
   - Figma password-reset screens and the "Super Admin" label must then be mapped onto it.
2. **`bk-001` scope:** the first slice above, versus the whole ERD v2 as AA-678's Done-when literally says.
3. **Booking API hostname and certificate** (`api-booking.lumiguides.it.com` or execute-api for Dev).
4. **Customer surface:** does Booking build PRD §7.3 Discovery, or does TripPlanner stay the discovery/inquiry front, with Booking's customer app limited to sign-in, My Trips and My Payments?
5. **Guest inquiries** (`customer: null` in the contract): park in `inbox_events` until contact data exists, or allow nullable `trip_cases.customer_id`.
6. **Content boundary for AAA-authored activities and country text:** commercial data owned by Booking, or content that must be authored in CIS (ADR 0002 "Revisit").
7. **Job kind prefix** (`bk_*` vs AA-751's `aab_*`).

## Consequences

- **Positive:**
  - one toolchain;
  - CI, deploy and done-rules are copied, not invented;
  - least-privilege DB and IAM from the first commit;
  - schema ownership is enforced by the database and the migration guard;
  - Dev cost is marginal (one small Fargate task on an existing cluster, ALB and NLB).
- **Negative / cost:**
  - Booking shares the CIS ALB, NLB, VPC link and RDS, so an incident or maintenance on those affects both apps;
  - path-prefix routing ties Booking's public paths to `/booking/*`;
  - grants depend on CIS and TripPlanner migrations, so cross-repo ordering must be planned;
  - the UI kit is copied until AA-655 ships;
  - the `bk-001` first slice means later `ALTER`s on an empty schema.

## Alternatives considered

- **Laravel/PHP**: the handover's "Spatie" permission tables suggest Quanskill's stack. Rejected: no code was delivered, and it would mean a second CI/deploy/auth path.
- **Lambda + HTTP API** (TripPlanner pattern). Rejected for the main API: OTP sessions, staff CRUD and a long-running consumer fit a container service, and CIS's ECS deploy and DB Migrate tooling already target ECS. It can be revisited for a stateless public read API.
- **Own ALB/NLB or own cluster.** Rejected for Dev (cost, more Terraform). Revisit for staging/prod isolation.
- **Host header routing on the existing ALB.** Rejected: API Gateway integrations call the NLB by DNS name, so the client's Host header does not reach the ALB.
- **Whole ERD v2 in `bk-001`.** Rejected (see decision 7).
- **Separate database or account.** Rejected by ADR 0001.
